newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends up despite funds inflows.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends up despite funds inflows.

text.p: Indian call money ended sharply up at 8.50 percent on Monday with most money market dealers unable to explain the reason for the rise.
Call money opened the day in the 6.50-7.0 percent range.
"It is quite confusing," said a dealer at a private bank. "Quite a lot of funds came in on the weekend and call rates should have been easier...It's actually quite worrying."

A half percentage point cut in banks' cash reserve ratio requirements by the Reserve Bank of India on Saturday released about 21 billion rupees while the reversal of a four-day repos conducted earlier last week released another 9.3 billion rupees.

One dealer said that call money rates could have firmed up due to local holidays in other parts of the country. With banks closed in some parts of India, it might not have been possible to get a clear picture of positions, he said.
This might have led to some panic borrowing, he said.
Dealers said the securities market was dull.
"With call money firming up, there was hardly any trade," a dealer said. "We should get a clearer position on Wednesday as everyone gets out of the holiday hangover."
Banks are closed in Bombay on Tuesday for a local holiday.
